description.label: API Description
description.text: Are you ready to unlock the full potential of E-commerceGo and seamlessly integrate it into your applications? Look no further. This comprehensive API documentation is your gateway to harnessing the power of E-commerceGo's features, allowing you to streamline your work, boost productivity, and bring your projects to the next level.

subdescription.label: Getting Started Description
subdescription.text: This API documentation is a resource for developers, both seasoned and new, who want to leverage E-commerceGo's capabilities within their applications. Here's what you can expect to find.

endpoint_description.label: EndPoints Description
endpoint_description.text: You can use HTTP methods like GET to retrieve data, POST to create new data, PUT to update existing data, and DELETE to remove data.

request_parameter_description.label: Request Parameter Description
request_parameter_description.text: Request parameters are used to customize the behavior of your API requests and provide more specific details when interacting with the API. For E-commerceGo, you might have the following types of request parameters:

request_parameter_sub_data.label: Request Parameter Sub Data
sub_description: You can use query parameters to filter or sort data when retrieving information. For example, you could use id to filter data within a specific id number.
Headers can be used for authentication and additional metadata about the request. For instance, you might need to include an Authorization header with an Bearer token for authentication.

When creating or updating data in E-commerceGo, you'll typically send a JSON request body. The request body will contain the data to be created or updated, such as users information, project information, or invoice information.

response_data_description.label: Response Data Description
response_data_description.text: E-commerceGo's API typically responds with data in JSON format

response_data_sub_data.label: Response Data SubData
sub_description: The response typically includes an HTTP status code indicating the outcome of the request (e.g., 200 for success, 404 for not found, 401 for unauthorized).
The actual data is contained within the 'data' field.
